implementation_constraints: reads entire stdin as one expression, tolerates leading/trailing whitespace and trailing newline
prints exactly the integer value or exactly ERROR, no other output

unresolved_intent.decision: zero-divisor is folded into the same ERROR path as parse errors (raised as ParseError and caught by the same handler)
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec only requires printing exactly ERROR for a zero divisor; it does not require distinguishing it from other unevaluable cases in the output, so a single error channel satisfies AC-PR-04/AC-PR-05 without added surface

unresolved_intent.decision: any character outside digits, whitespace, and + - * / ( ) is treated as a stray token and forces ERROR at the tokenize stage
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec defines the grammar as integers, + - * /, unary minus, and parentheses only; anything else has no defined meaning, so rejecting it satisfies the 'stray token -> ERROR' requirement (AC-PR-05) without guessing at unstated syntax

unresolved_intent.decision: a NUMBER token is a maximal run of ASCII digits (no sign, no leading-zero restriction, no size limit beyond Python's arbitrary-precision ints)
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec defines 'a non-negative integer literal' without further constraints; unary minus is a separate grammar rule applied to the parsed primary, so the tokenizer itself never consumes a sign, keeping negation and literals orthogonal as the spec's structure implies

unresolved_intent.decision: empty/whitespace-only input is detected after tokenization (zero tokens) rather than by checking the raw string length before tokenizing
unresolved_intent.rationale: this correctly classifies inputs that are only whitespace/newline as empty too (legal per spec's whitespace-tolerance rule), rather than treating them as some other kind of malformed input
